rows.name: intro_gamma_deriv
rows.doc: sec_01_intro.tex:7: "`Γ f(z) = (f(z) + z f'(z))/2 = ½ (z f(z))'`", at every point where `f` is differentiable.

rows.name: intro_gamma_coeff
rows.doc: sec_01_intro.tex:9: "`Γ` multiplies the coefficient `a_n` by `(n+1)/2`" (for `f ∈ 𝒮`, every `n`).

rows.name: intro_factor_two
rows.doc: sec_01_intro.tex:9: "`H = (zG)'`, which is `2 Γ G`; the factor does not affect univalence": on every set, `2 Γ f` is injective iff `Γ f` is. (`(zf)' = 2 Γ f` is `intro_gamma_deriv`.)

rows.name: intro_koebe_critical_on_circle
rows.doc: sec_01_intro.tex:9, :45 and sec_02_reduction.tex:23: the derivative of `Γ k` vanishes at `z = -½`, a point of the circle `|z| = ½` ("it allows critical points of `Γ f` on the circle `|z| = ½`, which occur for the Koebe function").

rows.name: sec2_f_ne
rows.doc: sec_02_reduction.tex:5: "For `f ∈ 𝒮` and distinct points `z, w ∈ 𝔻` we have `f(z) ≠ f(w)`".

rows.name: sec2_Q_symm
rows.doc: sec_02_reduction.tex:9: "The quotient `Q_f` is symmetric in `z` and `w`" (for every `f`, `z`, `w`).

rows.name: lem_2_1
rows.doc: Lemma 2.1 (sec_02_reduction.tex:11-17): for `f ∈ 𝒮` and distinct `z, w ∈ 𝔻`, `Γ f(z) - Γ f(w) = ½ (f(z) - f(w)) Q_f(z, w)`; in particular `Γ f(z) = Γ f(w)` iff `Q_f(z, w) = 0`.

rows.name: lem_2_2
rows.doc: Lemma 2.2 (sec_02_reduction.tex:25-27): let `ρ > 0` and let `G` be holomorphic on a neighbourhood of the closed disc `|z| ≤ ρ`. If `G` is injective on the circle `|z| = ρ`, then `G` is injective on the closed disc. PROVED GIVEN the argument principle and the Jordan curve theorem (Lean's library has neither).

rows.name: lem_2_3_rot
rows.doc: Lemma 2.3, rotation (sec_02_reduction.tex:39-40): for `f ∈ 𝒮` and real `φ`, the rotation `f_φ(z) = e^{-iφ} f(e^{iφ} z)` belongs to `𝒮`, and `Q_{f_φ}(z, w) = Q_f(e^{iφ} z, e^{iφ} w)` (for all `z, w ∈ 𝔻`).

rows.name: lem_2_3_dil
rows.doc: Lemma 2.3, dilation (sec_02_reduction.tex:40): for `f ∈ 𝒮` and `0 < r ≤ ½`, the dilation `F(u) = f(2ru)/(2r)` belongs to `𝒮`, and `Q_F(z, w) = Q_f(2rz, 2rw)` (for all `z, w ∈ 𝔻`).

rows.name: sec2_pair_normal_form
rows.doc: sec_02_reduction.tex:47-50: "Two distinct points on the circle `|z| = ½` have an angular distance `θ ∈ (0, π]`; after naming them suitably they are `z = ½ e^{i(φ + θ/2)}` and `w = ½ e^{i(φ - θ/2)}` for some real `φ`. By Lemma 2.3, `Q_f(z, w) = Q_{f_φ}(z_θ, \overline{z_θ})`."

rows.name: sec2_values_eq
rows.doc: sec_02_reduction.tex:51: "So the values of `Q_f` on pairs of distinct points of the circle, over all `f ∈ 𝒮`, are exactly the values `Q_f(z_θ, \overline{z_θ})`, over all `f ∈ 𝒮` and `0 < θ ≤ π`."

rows.name: prop_2_4
rows.doc: Proposition 2.4 (sec_02_reduction.tex:53-55): suppose that `Re Q_f(z_θ, \overline{z_θ}) > 0` for every `f ∈ 𝒮` and every `θ ∈ (0, π]`. Then Theorems 1.1 and 1.2 hold (the sharpness of `1/2` in Theorem 1.1 is the Koebe function, Proposition 2.5). PROVED GIVEN the facts of Lemma 2.2.

rows.name: koebe_mem_S
rows.doc: The Koebe function belongs to `𝒮` (used by sec_01_intro.tex:9, sec_02_reduction.tex:61-68 and Theorem 1.1's "sharp").

rows.name: prop_2_5
rows.doc: Proposition 2.5 (sec_02_reduction.tex:63-69): for the Koebe function `k(z) = z/(1-z)²`, `Γ k(z) = z/(1-z)³` and `(Γ k)'(z) = (1 + 2z)/(1-z)⁴` (in `𝔻`); hence `(Γ k)'(-½) = 0`, and `Γ k` is not injective on `𝔻_r` for any `r > ½`.

rows.name: sec2_koebe_limit
rows.doc: sec_02_reduction.tex:75 (and sec_01_intro.tex:73): "as `z` and `w` tend to `-½` along the circle, `Q_k(z, w)` tends to `0`. In the normalized position this happens for the rotation `k_π(z) = -k(-z)` as `θ → 0`."

rows.name: sec3_deriv_ne_zero
rows.doc: sec_03_tools.tex:13: "`f'(a) ≠ 0` because `f` is injective" (for `f ∈ 𝒮` and every `a ∈ 𝔻`).

rows.name: sec3_koebe_transform_mem_S
rows.doc: sec_03_tools.tex:9-13: for `f ∈ 𝒮` and `a ∈ 𝔻` the Koebe transform `f_a` again belongs to `𝒮`.

rows.name: sec3_kernel_nonvanishing
rows.doc: sec_03_tools.tex:24: for `g ∈ 𝒮`, `(g(s) - g(t))/(s - t)`, extended by `g'(s)` on the diagonal, has no zero on `𝔻 x 𝔻` and equals `1` at the origin, "and so does `g(s)/s` on `𝔻`" (extended by `g'(0) = 1` at `s = 0`).

rows.name: sec3_grunsky_exists
rows.doc: sec_03_tools.tex:24-28: for `g ∈ 𝒮` the Grunsky kernel `K_g` is a holomorphic function on `𝔻 x 𝔻` that vanishes when `s = 0` or `t = 0`, with coefficients `γ_{nm} = γ_{mn}`: Grunsky coefficients exist and are symmetric. PROVED GIVEN the power series of holomorphic functions on the bidisc.

rows.name: sec3_grunsky_unique
rows.doc: sec_03_tools.tex:28 ("the Grunsky coefficients of `g`"): two families with the property `IsGrunskyCoeff g` agree, so the predicate names the paper's coefficients.

rows.name: sec3_cauchy
rows.doc: sec_03_tools.tex:32-35 (eq:cauchy): "In particular, for all `x, y ∈ ℓ²`, `|xᵀ C(g) y| ≤ ‖x‖ ‖y‖`" (the bilinear form as iterated sums, which converge). PROVED GIVEN the strong Grunsky inequality.

rows.name: sec3_blocks_compressions
rows.doc: sec_03_tools.tex:36: "The same bound holds for every principal block of `C(g)` and for every compression `Vᵀ C(g) V` by a matrix `V` with orthonormal columns" (a principal block: rows and columns in a set `S`; `k` columns in `ℓ²`). PROVED GIVEN the strong Grunsky inequality.

rows.name: sec3_oddroot_exists
rows.doc: sec_03_tools.tex:39-43: for `f ∈ 𝒮` the odd square root `h(s) = √(f(s²))` exists.

rows.name: sec3_oddroot_mem_S
rows.doc: sec_03_tools.tex:43: "`h ∈ 𝒮`".

rows.name: sec3_oddroot_parity
rows.doc: sec_03_tools.tex:43: "Because `h` is odd, `K_h(-s, -t) = K_h(s, t)`, so `γ_{nm}(h) = 0` unless `n + m` is even."

rows.name: sec3_OE_contractions
rows.doc: sec_03_tools.tex:43: "The Grunsky matrix of `h` therefore splits into the block `O` of odd indices and the block `E` of even indices, and both are complex symmetric contractions" (contractions: every finite section). PROVED GIVEN the strong Grunsky inequality.

rows.name: sec3_block_sums
rows.doc: sec_03_tools.tex:45-47: "`∑_{n,m odd} γ_{nm}(h) sⁿ tᵐ = a(s)ᵀ O a(t)`, and similarly for the even indices".

rows.name: sec3_p_ne_zero
rows.doc: sec_03_tools.tex:49-51: for `f ∈ 𝒮`, `p(z) = z f'(z)/f(z)` is holomorphic on `𝔻`, "has no zero in `𝔻` and equals `1` at `z = 0`".

rows.name: lem_3_1_i
rows.doc: Lemma 3.1(i) (sec_03_tools.tex:56-57): `2 a(s)ᵀ O a(t) = K_h(s, t) - K_h(s, -t)`, and for `s ≠ ±t`, `exp(2 a(s)ᵀ O a(t)) = ((h(s) - h(t))/(h(s) + h(t))) · ((s + t)/(s - t))`.

rows.name: lem_3_1_ii
rows.doc: Lemma 3.1(ii) (sec_03_tools.tex:58): `2 a_e(s)ᵀ E a_e(t) = K_h(s, t) + K_h(s, -t) = K_f(z, w)` (`z = s²`, `w = t²`; `γf` the Grunsky coefficients of `f`).

rows.name: lem_3_1_iii
rows.doc: Lemma 3.1(iii) (sec_03_tools.tex:59): `log p(z) = 2 a(s)ᵀ O a(s)` (`z = s²`), the logarithm vanishing at `0`: the function `s ↦ 2 a(s)ᵀ O a(s)` is continuous on `𝔻`, vanishes at `0`, and its exponential is `p(s²)`.

rows.name: eq_Kf
rows.doc: sec_03_tools.tex:67-70 (eq:Kf): "the even block is the Grunsky matrix of `f` itself: `E_{2n,2m} = √(nm) γ_{nm}(f)`", and `K_f(z, w) = α(z)ᵀ C(f) α(w)` for `z, w ∈ 𝔻`.

rows.name: eq_gram
rows.doc: sec_03_tools.tex:72-79 (eq:gram): on `|s|² = ½` (`z = s²`): `‖a(s)‖² = artanh ½`, `a(s)ᵀ a(s) = artanh z`, `‖a_e(s)‖² = -½ log ¾`, `a_e(s)ᵀ a_e(s) = -½ log(1 - z²)`.

rows.name: sec4_midpoint
rows.doc: sec_04_near.tex:36-48, the pair seen from its midpoint: for `θ ∈ (0, π]`, `τ = ½ cos(θ/2)`, `y = ½ sin(θ/2)`: `z_θ = τ + iy`, `τ² + y² = ¼`, `g(z) = -f(-z)` (the rotation of Lemma 2.3 with `φ = π`), `Q_f(z_θ, \overline{z_θ}) = Q_g(-τ - iy, -τ + iy)`, `sin²(θ/2)/80 = y²/20`, and `θ ≤ θ₀ ⇔ y ≤ y₀`.

rows.name: sec4_goal_equiv
rows.doc: sec_04_near.tex:40-47: Proposition 4.1 is equivalent to (sec4:goal): `Re Q_f(-τ + iy, -τ - iy) ≥ y²/20` for `f ∈ 𝒮` and `0 < y ≤ y₀ = 17/80`, `τ = √(¼ - y²)` ("As `f ↦ g` is a bijection of `𝒮` and `Q` is symmetric", sec_04_near.tex:44, with `g(z) = -f(-z)`).

rows.name: sec4_c_bounds
rows.doc: sec_04_near.tex:53-60: for `f ∈ 𝒮` and `9/20 < τ < ½`, the Koebe transform `f_{-τ}` belongs to `𝒮`; with `A = a₂(f_{-τ})`, de Branges for `n = 2` gives `|A| ≤ 2`; `c = A/2` has `|c| ≤ 1`, `e ∈ [0, 4]`, `η ∈ [0, 1]`. PROVED GIVEN de Branges' theorem.

rows.name: sec4_eta_le
rows.doc: sec_04_near.tex:69: "Since `Re c = 1 - e/2` and `|c| ≥ |Re c|`, we have `η ≤ e - e²/4`. In particular `e = 0` forces `c = 1`, `η = 0`" (for `|c| ≤ 1`).

rows.name: sec4_model_mem_S
rows.doc: sec_04_near.tex:108 and sec_01_intro.tex:73: for `|c| ≤ 1` the comparison function `u/(1 - cu)²` belongs to `𝒮`, equals `k(cu)/c` for `c ≠ 0`, has second coefficient `2c`, and is the Koebe function when `c = 1`.

rows.name: sec4_hat_bounds
rows.doc: sec_04_near.tex:112 and :120: `ν(ν + 2β) = (c² - τ²)/v²`; for `9/20 ≤ τ ≤ ½` and `|c| ≤ 1`: `|ν| ≤ 1/(1 - τ) ≤ 2`, `|ν(ν + 2β)| ≤ (1 + τ²)/v² ≤ 20/9`, `y² = ¼ - τ² ≤ 19/400`; the denominators in (sec4:hat) stay away from `0` and `Q̂`, `T̂` (and `Π̂_o(iy)`) are holomorphic in `c` on a neighbourhood of `|c| ≤ 1`.

rows.name: eq_Qk
rows.doc: sec_04_near.tex:121-124 (eq:Qk): for `9/20 ≤ τ < ½`: `Q̂(τ, 1) = Q_k(τ) = y²/((½ + τ) · ¾ · (5/4 + 2τ)) ≥ (16/27) y²`, and it is the quotient of the Koebe function itself at the pair `-τ ± iy`.

rows.name: sec4_circle
rows.doc: sec_04_near.tex:139-147 (sec4:circle), the boundary step of Lemma 4.3: for `9/20 ≤ τ < ½`, `|c| = 1`, `x = Re c`, `e = 2(1 - x)`: `Re Q̂ ≥ Q_k + (13/10)e - (21/200)e² = Q_k + (1 - x)(109/50 + (21/50)x)`.

rows.name: lem_4_4_iv
rows.doc: Lemma 4.4(iv) (sec_04_near.tex:181-185): for `9/20 ≤ τ ≤ ½` with `0 < y ≤ y₀`, `|c| ≤ 1`, and a cap `|ν| ≤ ν⁺ ≤ 2` (as printed): `|T̂| ≤ T⁺` and `|Π̂_o(iy)| ≥ Π̂₋`.

rows.name: lem_4_5_i
rows.doc: Lemma 4.5(i) (sec_04_near.tex:220-228): for `9/20 ≤ τ < ½` and `|c| ≤ 1`, with `T_j` the printed closed form (`ξ = iy`), `∑_{j=2}^{5} |T_j|²/(2j - 1) ≤ 20 + 130e`.

rows.name: sec4_caps_valid
rows.doc: sec_04_near.tex:330: "The numbers in Lemma 4.8 are the caps of Lemmas 4.5 and 4.6 for a cell ...; by Lemma 4.7 and (sec4:rho), they are valid for every `f` whose `ρ` lies in the cell": for `9/20 ≤ τ ≤ ½`, `|c| ≤ 1`, `c ≠ 1` and `ρ = η/e ∈ [i/256, (i+1)/256]`: `|ν| ≤ ν⁺ ≤ 2`, `η ≤ η⁺ ≤ 1`, `e ≤ e⁺`, `(M + 130e)^{1/2} ≤ n⁺`.

rows.name: sec4_no_constant
rows.doc: sec_04_near.tex:31: the Koebe quotient is of the exact order `sin²(θ/2)` for nearby points (for `k_π`, in the normal position), so the bound of Proposition 4.1 cannot hold with a fixed positive constant in place of `sin²(θ/2)/80`.

rows.name: sec4_Gtau
rows.doc: sec_04_near.tex:61-65: since `f_{-τ}(u)/u` has no zero in `𝔻`, `G_τ(ζ) = (f_{-τ}(ζ⁻²))^{-1/2} = ζ - cζ⁻¹ + ∑_{j ≥ 2} b_{2j-1} ζ^{1-2j}` (`|ζ| > 1`, the branch like `ζ` at infinity) is holomorphic and odd, and it is injective. Typed with the unique square root `φ` of `u/f_{-τ}(u)` with `φ(0) = 1` and `G_τ(ζ) = ζ φ(ζ⁻²)`.

rows.name: sec4_area
rows.doc: (sec4:area), sec_04_near.tex:65-68: the area theorem for `G_τ` reads `|c|² + ∑_{j ≥ 2} (2j - 1)|b_{2j-1}|² ≤ 1`, that is, `∑_{j ≥ 2} (2j - 1)|b_{2j-1}|² ≤ η`.

rows.name: sec4_e_zero
rows.doc: sec_04_near.tex:69-70: "`e = 0` forces `c = 1`, `η = 0` and `b_{2j-1} = 0` for all `j`, that is, `f_{-τ} = k`".

rows.name: sec4_Pi_formula
rows.doc: (sec4:Pi), sec_04_near.tex:75-83: the automorphism `u ↦ (u - τ)/(1 - τu)` sends `u = ξ/(v + τξ)` to `-τ + ξ`, so `Π(ξ) = v f_{-τ}(ξ/(v + τξ))`; `Π = N/L²` with `N = ξ(1 + βξ)`, `L = 1 - νξ + B`; `π₁ = 1`, `π₂ = (2c - τ)/v`. Typed on `|ξ| < 1/4` (the paper: "for small ξ"; `y ≤ y₀ < 1/4`), with `Π L² = N`.

rows.name: lem_4_2
rows.doc: Lemma 4.2 (sec_04_near.tex:85-93): with `Π_o(ξ) = (Π(ξ) - Π(-ξ))/(2ξ)`, `D = 2(1 - 2τc)/v` and `Υ`, `Q_f(-τ + ξ, -τ - ξ) = D + ξ² Υ(ξ)/Π_o(ξ)`; at `ξ = iy`, (sec4:QDT) `Q_f(-τ + iy, -τ - iy) = D - y²T`. Typed for `0 < |ξ| < 1/4` (the paper, sec_04_near.tex:75: "For small ξ").

rows.name: sec4_D_diagonal
rows.doc: sec_04_near.tex:105: "The number `D = 2 + zf''(z)/f'(z)` at `z = -τ` is the diagonal value of `Q_f`. For fixed `τ` it depends only on `c`, and so does `π₂`" (`D = 2 - 2τπ₂`).

rows.name: sec4_hat_closed
rows.doc: sec_04_near.tex:107-119: for the comparison function (`b_{2j-1} = 0`, `Π̂ = N/(1 - νξ)²`): `π̂₁ = 1`, `π̂₂ = π₂`, and `Π̂_o(iy)`, `T̂`, `Q̂ = D - y²T̂` have the closed forms (sec4:hat).

rows.name: sec4_diff
rows.doc: (sec4:diff), sec_04_near.tex:108-110: "As `D` and `π₂` depend only on `c`, `Q_f(-τ + iy, -τ - iy) - Q̂ = -y²(T - T̂)`."

rows.name: sec4_majorant_split
rows.doc: sec_04_near.tex:153-156 (used in the proof of Proposition 4.1, sec_04_near.tex:337-341): "Split `T - T̂ = Ṫ + (T - T̂ - Ṫ)` ...; then `Re Q_f(-τ + iy, -τ - iy) ≥ Re Q̂ - y²|Ṫ| - y²|T - T̂ - Ṫ|`."

rows.name: sec4_majorant_rules
rows.doc: sec_04_near.tex:159: for `F ≪ Z`: `|F(ξ)| ≤ Z(|ξ|)` wherever `Z` converges; the relation is preserved by sums and products; and `(1 - F)⁻¹ ≪ (1 - Z)⁻¹` if `F(0) = Z(0) = 0` (the inverses are the solutions of `g = 1 + F g`, `G = 1 + Z G`).

rows.name: sec4_hw_coeff
rows.doc: sec_04_near.tex:164-169: for a majorant `Z` with `Z₁ = Z₂ = 0`, in terms of coefficients `𝔥[Z] = ∑_{j ≥ 1} Z_{2j+1} x^{2j}` and `𝔴[Z] = ∑_{j ≥ 1} [(2j + 10/3)Z_{2j+1} + (j+1)Z_{2j+2}] x^{2j-2}`; both increase with `x ≥ 0` (inside the disc of convergence).

rows.name: lem_4_4_i
rows.doc: Lemma 4.4(i) (sec_04_near.tex:174): if `ΔΠ = ∑_{n ≥ 3} Δπ_n ξⁿ ≪ Z` and `ΔΠ_o`, `ΔΥ` are formed from the `Δπ_n` by the linear rules of Lemma 4.2 with `π₂ = (2c - τ)/v` kept fixed, then `|ΔΠ_o(iy)| ≤ 𝔥[Z](y)` and `|ΔΥ(iy)| ≤ 𝔴[Z](y)` (`Z` converging at `y`, with the derivative-type weights).

rows.name: lem_4_4_ii
rows.doc: Lemma 4.4(ii) (sec_04_near.tex:175): for every `f ∈ 𝒮`, `|Π_o(iy) - 1| ≤ ε(y)`.

rows.name: lem_4_4_iii
rows.doc: Lemma 4.4(iii) (sec_04_near.tex:176-179): `B ≪ √η B₁` and `B² ≪ η B₂` (coefficients in `ξ`).

rows.name: sec4_first_variation
rows.doc: sec_04_near.tex:212-216 (the first variation): with `B` replaced by `λB`, `Π̇ = -2NB/(1 - νξ)³ = ∑_{j ≥ 2} b_{2j-1} Π_j` and `Ṫ = ∑_{j ≥ 2} b_{2j-1} T_j` (the derivative at `λ = 0` of `T` computed from `N/(1 - νξ + λB)²`); at `λ = 1` this is `Π`, at `λ = 0` the comparison function `Π̂`. Typed with complex `λ` (`T` is holomorphic in `λ`): stronger than the printed real `0 ≤ λ ≤ 1`, and true.

rows.name: sec4_Tj_closed
rows.doc: sec_04_near.tex:216: "where `T_j = (Υ_j - T̂ Π_{j,o})/Π̂_o`, with `Υ_j` and `Π_{j,o}` formed from `Π_j` by the linear rules of Lemma 4.2 (`π₂` kept fixed)", and differentiating the first formula of Lemma 4.2's proof "gives the closed form used in Lemma 4.5" (`Υ_j`, `Π_{j,o}` by the linear rules with `π₂` fixed).

rows.name: sec4_low_coeffs
rows.doc: Lemma 4.4(i), its last sentence (sec_04_near.tex:174) and its proof (:190): two functions of the form (sec4:Pi) with the same `τ` and `c` have the same `π₀ = 0`, `π₁ = 1` and `π₂`, so their difference starts at `ξ³`; so does each derivative `Π_j` with respect to `b_{2j-1}`.

rows.name: sec4_majorant_conv
rows.doc: sec_04_near.tex:159 and :267: the denominators of the majorants, `1 - ⅔x`, `1 - 2x`, `𝔞 = 1 - ν⁺x` (`ν⁺ ≤ 2`) and `𝔡 = 𝔞 - √η⁺ B₁` (`η⁺ ≤ 1`), stay positive for `|x| ≤ 1/4`, with `𝔡(1/4) ≥ 1/2 - 2/15`; `1 - 𝔡 = ν⁺x + √η⁺B₁` has nonnegative coefficients (those of `B₁`), "so they converge for `|x| ≤ 1/4`".

rows.name: lem_4_5_ii
rows.doc: Lemma 4.5(ii) (sec_04_near.tex:229-233; `𝔥`, `𝔴` as at sec_04_near.tex:159-163): if moreover `0 < y ≤ y₀` and `|ν| ≤ ν⁺ ≤ 2` (as printed), then `(∑_{j ≥ 6} |T_j|²/(2j - 1))^{1/2} ≤ N₆`.

rows.name: lem_4_5_iii
rows.doc: Lemma 4.5(iii) (sec_04_near.tex:234): under the hypotheses of (ii), `|Ṫ| ≤ √η √(M + 130e)`, `M = 20 + N₆²`.

rows.name: sec4_Lam_nonneg
rows.doc: A step of the proof of Proposition 4.1 (sec_04_near.tex:342): `Λ ≥ 0` on every cell, so `ρ e Λ ≤ ρ₊ e Λ`. The paper names it there: "`Λ ≥ 0` (the series in `Λ` have nonnegative coefficients, `T⁺, n⁺ ≥ 0` and `Π₋ > 0`)"; the majorants have nonnegative coefficients by sec_04_near.tex:159. SUPPORT row (the paper's own step).

rows.name: prop_4_1_from_layer
rows.doc: The proof of Proposition 4.1 (sec_04_near.tex:336-346), as an implication: from the case `e = 0` (`Q_f = Q_k`) and the per-cell bound `Re Q_f ≥ (16/27)y² + e m(ρ) - y²√(ρe(M + 130e)) - y²ρeΛ` (its first display, with the cell's numbers), Lemma 4.8 gives (sec4:goal), hence Proposition 4.1. The proof uses `|c| ≤ 1` (de Branges for `n = 2`, sec_04_near.tex:57) to place `ρ` in a cell and `e ≤ e⁺`, hence the binder `hDB`.

rows.name: sec5_s_sq
rows.doc: sec_05_grunsky_q.tex:8-10: `s = 2^{-1/2} e^{iθ/4}`, `t = s̄`, "so that `s² = z` and `t² = w`".

rows.name: sec5_coords
rows.doc: sec_05_grunsky_q.tex:13-19, the coordinates: for `θ ∈ (0, π]`, `l₁₁ > 0`, `l₂₂ > 0` (`u`, `v` are linearly independent), and `ũ, ṽ` have the Gram matrix of `u, v`: `l₁₁² = (A_o + Re Z_o)/2`, `l₁₁ l₂₁ = Im Z_o / 2`, `l₂₁² + l₂₂² = (A_o - Re Z_o)/2`.

facts.name: Robinson.FactArgumentPrinciple
facts.doc: NOT FORMALIZED: no argument principle in Lean's library. The argument principle [Ahl79, Chapter 4, Section 5.2] as sec_02_reduction.tex:30 uses it: if `G` is holomorphic on a neighbourhood of `|z| ≤ ρ` and `G - c` has no zero on the circle `|z| = ρ`, then `G - c` has finitely many zeros in `|z| < ρ`, each of finite order, and their number counted with multiplicity, `N(c)`, equals the winding number `ind_J(c)` of the image curve about `c`.

facts.name: Robinson.FactJordanCurve
facts.doc: NOT FORMALIZED: no Jordan curve theorem in Lean's library. The Jordan curve theorem with winding numbers, as sec_02_reduction.tex:30 uses it: if `G` is holomorphic on a neighbourhood of `|z| ≤ ρ` and injective on the circle `|z| = ρ`, then its image `J` is a Jordan curve; `ℂ \ J` is the disjoint union of a bounded component `Ω` and an unbounded component `Ω'` (connected open sets); `J` is the boundary of `Ω'`; `ind_J = 0` on `Ω'`, and `ind_J` is a constant `ε ∈ {1, -1}` on `Ω`. Sources, as sec_02_reduction.tex:30 cites them: [HS18, Corollaries 1.4 and 1.6] (Hemasundar and Simha: the two components, and `J` is the boundary of each), [Ahl79, Chapter 4, Section 2.1] (the winding number is `0` on the unbounded component and constant on each component) and [HS18, Theorem 3.2] (its value on `Ω` is `1` or `-1`).

facts.name: Robinson.FactDeBranges
facts.doc: NOT FORMALIZED: no univalent-function theory in Lean's library. De Branges' theorem [deB85], as sec_03_tools.tex:13-16 states it: the coefficients of every `f(z) = z + ∑_{n ≥ 2} a_n z^n` in `𝒮` satisfy `|a_n| ≤ n` for `n ≥ 2`.

facts.name: Robinson.FactArea
facts.doc: NOT FORMALIZED: no univalent-function theory in Lean's library. The area theorem of Gronwall [Gro14], [Dur83, Chapter 2], as sec_03_tools.tex:17-20 states it: if `g(ζ) = ζ + b₀ + ∑_{n ≥ 1} b_n ζ^{-n}` is holomorphic and injective in `|ζ| > 1`, then `∑_{n ≥ 1} n |b_n|² ≤ 1`.

facts.name: Robinson.FactGrunsky
facts.doc: NOT FORMALIZED: no univalent-function theory in Lean's library. The strong Grunsky inequality [Gru39], [Pom75, Theorem 3.1], as sec_03_tools.tex:28-35 states it: for `g ∈ 𝒮` the matrix `C(g) = (√(nm) γ_{nm})` is an operator on `ℓ²` of norm at most `1`; in the bilinear form (eq:cauchy) `|xᵀ C(g) y| ≤ ‖x‖ ‖y‖`, here for every finite section (`x, y` supported on `n < N`, every `N`), which is equivalent to the norm bound.

facts.name: Robinson.FactBidiscPowerSeries
facts.doc: NOT FORMALIZED: no holomorphic functions of several variables in Lean's library. The power series of a holomorphic function on the bidisc (Osgood's lemma and the Cauchy formula on a polydisc), as sec_03_tools.tex:24-28 uses it for the Grunsky kernel: a function continuous on `𝔻 x 𝔻` and holomorphic in each variable separately is the sum of a double power series `∑ c_{nm} sⁿ tᵐ` that converges absolutely on all of `𝔻 x 𝔻`. Source, as sec_03_tools.tex:28 cites it: [Hor90, Section 2.2] (Hörmander).
